title: Update Track Popularity Tier by Streams
prompt: You are managing a music streaming service that tracks saved tracks across users. Each track has a `popularity_tier` that needs to be updated based on the total number of times it has been streamed. Write a single UPDATE statement that sets the `popularity_tier` column according to these rules: if a track has been streamed 1000 or more times, set `popularity_tier` to `'viral'`; if it has been streamed between 500 and 999 times (inclusive), set `popularity_tier` to `'popular'`; if it has been streamed between 100 and 499 times (inclusive), set `popularity_tier` to `'rising'`; otherwise (fewer than 100 streams), set `popularity_tier` to `'niche'`. Use a CASE expression in your SET clause. After the UPDATE, include a SELECT statement that returns all columns from the tracks table ordered by `stream_count` descending, then by `track_id` ascending.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE tracks (track_id INT PRIMARY KEY, track_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, artist_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, stream_count INT NOT NULL, popularity_tier VARCHAR(20));

composite_moves: row-transform: conditional tier assignment using CASE in UPDATE SET clause

hints: You need to update every row in the tracks table based on the stream_count value.
Use a CASE expression in your SET clause to assign different tier values based on stream_count thresholds (1000+, 500-999, 100-499, <100).

The UPDATE statement should be: UPDATE tracks SET popularity_tier = CASE WHEN stream_count >= 1000 THEN 'viral' WHEN stream_count >= 500 THEN 'popular' WHEN stream_count >= 100 THEN 'rising' ELSE 'niche' END; followed by SELECT * FROM tracks ORDER BY stream_count DESC, track_id ASC;
answer_key:
UPDATE tracks
SET popularity_tier = CASE
  WHEN stream_count >= 1000 THEN 'viral'
  WHEN stream_count >= 500 THEN 'popular'
  WHEN stream_count >= 100 THEN 'rising'
  ELSE 'niche'
END;

SELECT * FROM tracks ORDER BY stream_count DESC, track_id ASC;
